claims.text: Controlled pre-straining of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi coatings produces a higher initial defect density.
A higher initial defect density accelerates and enhances shear-induced dynamic transformations during sliding.
The proposed transformation consists of localized amorphization followed by recrystallization into an ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer.
Formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer is linked to low friction and high wear resistance in CoCrFeMnNi.
Magnetron sputtering yields a fine-grained CoCrFeMnNi coating with low initial defect density for the baseline.
A tailored thermal pretreatment can selectively increase dislocation density and alter grain-boundary stability.
Sliding can generate a nanocrystalline or ultra-nanocrystalline tribological layer through dynamic grain refinement.
Dislocations introduced by pre-straining concentrate shear stress and thereby trigger localized dynamic amorphization.
Localized dynamic amorphization is followed by recrystallization under wear conditions.
The resulting ultra-nanocrystalline layer dissipates energy.
The resulting ultra-nanocrystalline layer reduces friction.
The resulting ultra-nanocrystalline layer impedes crack initiation and propagation.
Pre-strained coatings will form the ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer earlier and more uniformly than untreated coatings.
Pre-strained coatings will exhibit lower friction coefficients than untreated coatings.
Pre-strained coatings will exhibit lower wear rates than untreated coatings.
The predicted reductions in friction and wear will persist across normal loads from approximately 1 N to 10 N.
Untreated CoCrFeMnNi coatings form the shear-induced layer more slowly or less uniformly during wear.
The mechanism is expected to apply during room-temperature dry sliding in an inert atmosphere.
Oxidation can substantially affect deformation and wear behavior, so the hypothesis may not apply under oxidizing conditions.
CoCrFeMnNi exhibits dynamic amorphization and formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer under sliding in a nonreactive environment.
